title: Encore - Living a happy single life, with Geoff MacDonald, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a winter break, so we're rerunning one of our favorite episodes
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》节目正在进行寒假休刊，因此我们重播了一期我们最喜欢的往期节目。

sentences.en: from the paSt. In 2022, I talked to psychologist Jeff McDonald about how more Americans are single than ever before, and many of them are happy to stay that way.
sentences.zh: 在2022年，我与心理学家杰夫·麦克唐纳（Jeff McDonald）探讨了为何如今单身的美国人比以往任何时候都多，而且许多人乐于保持这种状态。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望您喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with new episodes in January.
sentences.zh: 关于《心理学谈话》，我们将在1月份带着新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: We talk a lot on this podcast about relationships, and there's no doubt that relationships can be an important driver of many people's health, happiness, and well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们在本播客中经常谈论人际关系，毫无疑问，人际关系可以成为许多人健康、幸福和福祉的重要驱动力。

sentences.en: But focusing solely on partnerships or romantic relationships misses a crucial fact.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅关注伴侣关系或恋爱关系会忽略一个关键事实。

sentences.en: More Americans than ever before are single, and many are perfectly happy to stay that way.
sentences.zh: 如今单身的美国人比以往任何时候都多，而且许多人非常乐于保持单身。

sentences.en: A 2019 Pew Research Center poll found that 3 in 10 U.S.
sentences.zh: 皮尤研究中心（Pew Research Center）2019年的一项民意调查发现，十分之三的美国

sentences.en: adults are single.
sentences.zh: 成年人是单身。

sentences.en: They're not married, living with a partner, or in a committed relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们没有结婚，没有与伴侣同居，也没有处于承诺关系中。

sentences.en: Among those singles, half said they were not interested in dating or looking for a relationship.
sentences.zh: 在这些单身人士中，有一半表示他们对约会或寻找伴侣不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, looking simply at marriage rates, we find the number of singles is even higher.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，仅从结婚率来看，我们发现单身人数甚至更高。

sentences.en: According to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 根据美国

sentences.en: Census
sentences.zh: 人口普查

sentences.en: Bureau, about 50% of American adults are unmarried, or close to 127 million people.
sentences.zh: 局的数据，约50%的美国成年人未婚，即接近1.27亿人。

sentences.en: Those singles are a diverse bunch.
sentences.zh: 这些单身人士是一个多元化的群体。

sentences.en: Some have never been married.
sentences.zh: 有些人从未结过婚。

sentences.en: Some are divorced.
sentences.zh: 有些人离过婚。

sentences.en: Some widowed.
sentences.zh: 有些人丧偶。

sentences.en: They are older or younger.
sentences.zh: 他们有老有少。

sentences.en: Some are parents.
sentences.zh: 有些人是父母。

sentences.en: Others have no children.
sentences.zh: 另一些人没有孩子。

sentences.en: All of those factors, and many others, may affect how people experience singlehood.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素以及许多其他因素，都可能影响人们对单身生活的体验。

sentences.en: So how is relationship status related to well-being?
sentences.zh: 那么，恋爱状态与幸福感有何关联？

sentences.en: What makes some people happy with singlehood while others are not?
sentences.zh: 是什么让一些人对单身感到满意，而另一些人却不然？

sentences.en: Is there a societal stigma against singles?
sentences.zh: 社会对单身人士是否存在偏见？

sentences.en: And if so, how does that stigma affect people's lives?
sentences.zh: 如果有，这种偏见如何影响人们的生活？

sentences.en: Why is there so much more research on being in a happy relationship than on being happily single?
sentences.zh: 为什么关于处于幸福关系中的研究比关于幸福单身的研究要多得多？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Jeff McDonald, a professor of psychology at the University of
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是多伦多大学的心理学教授杰夫·麦克唐纳博士。

sentences.en: Toronto.
sentences.zh: （多伦多大学）

sentences.en: He has studied aspects of relationships for many years, including attachment theory and intimacy.
sentences.zh: 他多年来一直研究人际关系的各个方面，包括依恋理论和亲密关系。

sentences.en: More recently, he turned his attention to singlehood, and today, the primary aim of his lab is to better understand well-being in singlehood.
sentences.zh: 最近，他将注意力转向了单身生活，今天，他实验室的主要目标是更好地了解单身状态下的幸福感。

sentences.en: His and his colleagues' research has started to create a portrait of what makes for a happy single person.
sentences.zh: 他和同事们的研究已经开始描绘出什么样的人会成为快乐的单身人士。

sentences.en: So I'm looking forward to talking today about that and much more.
sentences.zh: 所以我很期待今天能谈论这个话题以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me, Dr. McDonald.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我的节目，麦克唐纳博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I mentioned that you studied relationships for many years before you started studying singlehood.
sentences.zh: 我提到过您在开始研究单身生活之前，已经研究了多年的人际关系。

sentences.en: What made you turn your attention to single people, and why do you think it's important for researchers to study singlehood?
sentences.zh: 是什么让您将注意力转向单身人士？您认为研究单身生活对研究人员来说为什么很重要？

sentences.en: I mean, I think the primary driver in turning my attention to singlehood is just recognizing, you know, like you said at the top there, there are a lot of single people out there,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为将注意力转向单身生活的主要驱动力只是认识到，正如您刚才在开头所说，外面有很多单身人士，

sentences.en: and that number is increasing, not just in the United States, not just in Canada.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字正在增加，不仅是在美国，也不仅是在加拿大。

sentences.en: This seems to be a worldwide trend.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个全球性的趋势。

sentences.en: So it's something that's important to pay attention to, but we know really very little about who single people are and what makes single people happy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个值得关注的问题，但我们对单身人士是谁以及什么让他们快乐知之甚少。

sentences.en: And, you know, even if you just want to take this from the perspective of a relationship researcher, everybody is single before they get in their first relationship.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使您只是想从关系研究人员的角度来看，每个人在进入第一段关系之前都是单身。

sentences.en: Most of the time when you end a relationship, you end up single.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，当你结束一段关系时，你最终会变成单身。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's important to not think about this as two different groups of people, largely speaking.
sentences.zh: 所以，不要把这看作是两类不同的人，这很重要，从大范围来看。

sentences.en: These are different phases of most people's lives.
sentences.zh: 这些是大多数人生命中不同的阶段。

sentences.en: And so even if your goal is just to understand relationships, you need to understand singlehood.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使您的目标只是了解人际关系，您也需要了解单身生活。

sentences.en: But I think understanding single people is important in its own right.
sentences.zh: 但我认为了解单身人士本身就很重要。

sentences.en: A lot of research over the years has found evidence that on average, married people are happier, healthier, and generally have better life outcomes compared with single people.
sentences.zh: 多年来的大量研究发现，平均而言，与单身人士相比，已婚人士更快乐、更健康，并且通常有更好的生活结果。

sentences.en: But some researchers who study singlehood have pushed back against that idea.
sentences.zh: 但一些研究单身生活的研究人员反驳了这一观点。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 您怎么看？

sentences.en: Are partnered people generally better off than those who are single?
sentences.zh: 有伴侣的人通常比单身的人过得好吗？

sentences.en: Is that even the right question to ask?
sentences.zh: 这甚至是一个正确的问题吗？

sentences.en: I think it's one of the right questions to ask, but it's not the only one.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是正确的问题之一，但不是唯一的一个。

sentences.en: And, you know, I certainly think I should say off the top that this is such a young field of research.
sentences.zh: 而且，我当然认为我应该在开头说，这是一个非常年轻的研究领域。

sentences.en: So we have some initial things to say about it, but I think all of this is up for debate and discussion.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一些初步的看法，但我认为这一切都有待辩论和讨论。

sentences.en: You know, from my reading of the literature, I think it would be fair to say that the average person who is in a
sentences.zh: 根据我对文献的阅读，我认为可以公平地说，处于

sentences.en: romantic relationship is higher in well-being, they're happier, they're higher in life satisfaction than the average person who is single.
sentences.zh: 恋爱关系中的普通人，其幸福感更高，他们更快乐，生活满意度也比普通单身人士更高。

sentences.en: But there's so much variability within each group.
sentences.zh: 但每个群体内部都有很大的差异。

sentences.en: Not every single person is miserable, and certainly not everybody in a relationship is ecstatic with their life.
sentences.zh: 并非每个单身人士都很痛苦，当然也不是每个处于关系中的人都对自己的生活感到狂喜。

sentences.en: So that's really been the focus of what we've been doing at our lab, and I think a lot of singlehood researchers have been doing, is, you know, looking at who are the
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我们实验室一直在做的事情的重点，我想很多单身研究人员也一直在做，那就是观察谁是

sentences.en: happier versus less happy single people to get a sense of, you know, which types of single people
sentences.zh: 更快乐与不那么快乐的单身人士，以了解哪些类型的单身人士

sentences.en: are doing really well for themselves, and which types of single people might not be doing so well.
sentences.zh: 过得很好，而哪些类型的单身人士可能过得不太好。

sentences.en: One of the central questions in your lab is what makes people happy or content with being single.
sentences.zh: 您实验室的核心问题之一是什么让人们对单身感到快乐或满足。

sentences.en: Are there common traits that happy singles share, personality traits or life circumstances or other things?
sentences.zh: 快乐的单身人士是否有共同的特质，比如人格特质、生活环境或其他方面？

sentences.en: There's a few things that we seem to be starting to put our finger on now.
sentences.zh: 现在我们似乎开始掌握了一些东西。

sentences.en: So one, for example, is that people who have never been married or people who have never been in a romantic relationship tend to be happier singles than people who have been.
sentences.zh: 例如，从未结过婚或从未有过恋爱关系的人，往往比有过这些经历的人更快乐。

sentences.en: We don't really have any direct evidence as to why that's the case, but my guess would be people know what's good for them.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有任何直接证据表明为什么会这样，但我的猜测是人们知道什么对自己好。

sentences.en: And there's a reason why some people don't choose to be in romantic relationships, because they know that's not what's going to make them happy.
sentences.zh: 有些人选择不进入恋爱关系是有原因的，因为他们知道那并不能让他们快乐。

sentences.en: And, you know, the flip side of that is that one of the groups that does less well with singlehood is people who've been through a divorce.
sentences.zh: 而且，反过来说，单身生活过得不太好的群体之一是经历过离婚的人。

sentences.en: There is some evidence that suggests that divorce can have a bit of a damaging effect on at least some people,
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，离婚至少对某些人可能会产生一定的破坏性影响，

sentences.en: which, you know, we think is particularly interesting because the bias tends to be that romantic relationships are good for people.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这特别有趣，因为偏见往往是恋爱关系对人有益。

sentences.en: But if you think about the way that people come out of divorce is maybe less well off than when they started, relationships can actually be damaging, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你考虑到人们离婚后的状态可能比开始时更糟糕，那么人际关系实际上可能是破坏性的，对吧？

sentences.en: But there's a reason that as a society, we haven't thought about relationships as damaging.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个社会，我们没有把人际关系视为破坏性的是有原因的。

sentences.en: The assumption is that they're good.
sentences.zh: 假设它们是好的。

sentences.en: So, you know, relationship history, I think, is an important one.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为人际关系史是一个重要的因素。

sentences.en: Generally speaking, the tack that I tend to take on this is that the people who are doing well in singlehood are sort of the people who are good at life in general.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我倾向于采取的观点是，那些在单身生活中过得好的人，通常是那些在生活中总体上过得好的人。

sentences.en: That, you know, people, for example, who are higher in attachment security.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，例如，那些依恋安全性更高的人。

sentences.en: So, these would be the kinds of people who are comfortable making close relationships with people and who are not really worried so much about getting rejected by other people.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些人是那种乐于与人建立亲密关系，并且不太担心被别人拒绝的人。

sentences.en: I mean, they do well in romantic relationships, but our evidence suggests that these are people who do well in singlehood as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在恋爱关系中表现得很好，但我们的证据表明，这些人同样也能过好单身生活。

sentences.en: Maybe one of the reasons for that is that people who are happier in singlehood are also people who
sentences.zh: 也许其中一个原因是，在单身生活中更快乐的人，也是那些

sentences.en: have good relationships with their friends and good relationships with their families.
sentences.zh: 与朋友关系良好、与家人关系良好的人。

sentences.en: And that skill set that comes with attachment security, the ability to be comfortably close
sentences.zh: 而那种伴随依恋安全性而来的技能，即能够舒适地与人亲近，

sentences.en: to people, to take emotional risks that allow you to get close to people, that's not just limited to romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 去承担允许你与人亲近的情感风险，这不仅仅局限于恋爱关系。

sentences.en: Those people are going to bring those kinds of skills to their friendships and their family relationships.
sentences.zh: 这些人会将这些技能带到他们的友谊和家庭关系中。

sentences.en: And I do think, you know, there's a bit of old-fashioned wisdom here that I think that some people have the idea that when you get into a romantic
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，这里有一些老派的智慧，我认为有些人有一种想法，即当你进入一段恋爱

sentences.en: relationship, that then you're going to become a happy person.
sentences.zh: 关系时，你就会变成一个快乐的人。

sentences.en: But when you understand the kinds of people who are happy single are also the kinds of people who are happy in relationships, it suggests
sentences.zh: 但当你了解那些快乐的单身人士也是那些在关系中快乐的人时，这表明

sentences.en: that maybe the best idea is to get right with yourself first and go towards a romantic relationship when you've done whatever that work is.
sentences.zh: 也许最好的主意是先让自己变得更好，当你完成了那些功课后，再走向一段恋爱关系。

sentences.en: Now, when you're studying people who are single, does that mean that they can't have relationships, that they can't have, you know, intimacy with other people?
sentences.zh: 那么，当您研究单身人士时，这是否意味着他们不能拥有人际关系，不能与他人拥有亲密关系？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly in terms of their friendship and their family relationships, there's lots of opportunity for intimacy there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然在他们的友谊和家庭关系方面，那里有很多亲密的机会。

sentences.en: One of the projects that we have ongoing in the lab right now is also looking at the romantic and sexual kinds of connections that single people have.
sentences.zh: 我们实验室目前正在进行的项目之一，也在观察单身人士所拥有的浪漫和性方面的联系。

sentences.en: So certainly, you know, over the last, like, however many decades, social norms have changed around opportunities for casual sexual opportunities or relationships that
sentences.zh: 所以当然，在过去的几十年里，围绕偶然性机会或关系的社会规范已经发生了变化，这些关系

sentences.en: sort of straddle the line between dating and not dating, like friends with benefits, for example.
sentences.zh: 介于约会和不约会之间，例如“炮友”。

sentences.en: Friends with benefits.
sentences.zh: 炮友。

sentences.en: That's what I was thinking, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是我所想的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, we know that there are a number of single people who tell us that they're sexually active, but we haven't really
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道有很多单身人士告诉我们他们有性生活，但我们还没有真正

sentences.en: collected the data yet on, well, what kinds of relationships are those?
sentences.zh: 收集到关于这些是什么样的关系的数据。

sentences.en: And so, we're, you know, we're trying to delve into that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正在尝试深入研究这一点。

sentences.en: What we do know is that single people who are higher in sexual satisfaction tend to be happier with singlehood.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，性满意度较高的单身人士往往对单身生活更满意。

sentences.en: But the other part of that is that the data suggests to us that singles who are happier with their sex lives are also more likely to end up in relationships down the road.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，数据向我们表明，对性生活更满意的单身人士也更有可能在未来进入恋爱关系。

sentences.en: And so, you know, one of our guesses about that is that, you know, being with people in sexual and romantic relationships, it's not like shopping for a
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对此的一个猜测是，在性关系和恋爱关系中与人相处，并不像购买

sentences.en: product where if you don't like it, you take it back.
sentences.zh: 产品，如果不喜欢就可以退货。

sentences.en: You know, the human heart works such that relationships are kind of sticky.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人心运作的方式使得人际关系有点粘人。

sentences.en: And even when you are in casual sexual relationships, for example, next thing you know, you're leaving a toothbrush.
sentences.zh: 即使你处于偶然的性关系中，例如，接下来你会发现自己留下了一把牙刷。

sentences.en: And next thing you know, you're leaving a set of pajamas.
sentences.zh: 接下来你会发现自己留下了一套睡衣。

sentences.en: And next thing you know, it's easier to just move in because you're already spending three nights a week there, right?
sentences.zh: 接下来你会发现，搬进去住更容易，因为你已经每周在那里过夜三个晚上了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, we think that even though sexual satisfaction is definitely something that's associated with happiness and singlehood, that might also indicate somebody who's
sentences.zh: 所以，我们认为尽管性满意度绝对是与单身幸福感相关联的，但这可能也预示着某人

sentences.en: on the road to being in a committed romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 正走在进入承诺恋爱关系的路上。

sentences.en: Let me ask how age affects people's experience of singlehood.
sentences.zh: 让我问一下年龄如何影响人们的单身体验。

sentences.en: Do people become more or less content with being single as they get older?
sentences.zh: 人们随着年龄的增长，对单身的满足感是增加了还是减少了？

sentences.en: So, our evidence suggests that there's, you know, kind of an inflection point around midlife,
sentences.zh: 我们的证据表明，在中年左右有一个转折点，

sentences.en: that single people starting at about age 40 start to become more satisfied with being single.
sentences.zh: 单身人士从40岁左右开始，对单身的满意度开始增加。

sentences.en: It's important to point out that's not unique to singlehood, that it looks like there's some
sentences.zh: 需要指出的是，这并非单身生活所独有，似乎有一些

sentences.en: evidence suggesting that well-being in general for people tends to increase after about midlife.
sentences.zh: 证据表明，人们的总体幸福感往往在中年之后增加。

sentences.en: So, there's another study by Janina Buehler where she looked at are people happy with the romantic relationships?
sentences.zh: 所以，Janina Buehler的另一项研究观察了人们是否对恋爱关系感到快乐？

sentences.en: And she found exactly the same pattern.
sentences.zh: 她发现了完全相同的模式。

sentences.en: Starting at about age 40, people start to become happier with the relationships.
sentences.zh: 从40岁左右开始，人们开始对关系感到更快乐。

sentences.en: So, you know, it kind of looks like around midlife, people start to become happier with the path that they've chosen.
sentences.zh: 所以，看起来在中年左右，人们开始对自己选择的道路感到更快乐。

sentences.en: I do think another factor in that, though, is some people who want to be in a relationship get selected out of the singles pool.
sentences.zh: 但我认为其中的另一个因素是，一些想要进入关系的人被从单身池中筛选出去了。

sentences.en: That if you're younger and you'd really like to be in a relationship, you're more likely to actually end up dating.
sentences.zh: 如果你更年轻，并且真的很想进入一段关系，你更有可能最终去约会。

sentences.en: And so, maybe part of the reason that older singles are happier being single is that there's going to be less of them in that pool who wish that they were in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许年长的单身人士对单身更快乐的部分原因是，在那个群体中，希望自己处于恋爱关系中的人会更少。

sentences.en: Now, having said that, in another study that we conducted, what the data looked like is that for older people who don't let go of wanting a
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，在我们进行的另一项研究中，数据显示，对于那些不放弃想要一段

sentences.en: relationship, like that variable of do you want to be in a romantic relationship or not, also seems to
sentences.zh: 关系的老年人来说，即“你是否想进入恋爱关系”这个变量，似乎也

sentences.en: be something that's important in understanding whether people are happy with being single or not,
sentences.zh: 是理解人们是否对单身感到快乐的重要因素，

sentences.en: that particularly older women who have let go of the desire or who never had a desire for a romantic
sentences.zh: 特别是那些已经放弃了对恋爱关系的渴望，或者从一开始就从未有过这种渴望的年长女性，

sentences.en: relationship in the first place are our highest group in terms of life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 是我们生活满意度最高的群体。

sentences.en: But it's the people who, as they get older, continue to wish that they were in a romantic relationship that seems to be associated with lower life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但那些随着年龄增长，仍然希望自己处于恋爱关系中的人，似乎与较低的生活满意度相关。

sentences.en: So, there's something about making peace with your circumstances, letting go of things that you can't have that might also be part of this process of
sentences.zh: 所以，与自己的处境和解，放下那些你无法拥有的东西，这可能是成为一个快乐的年长单身人士的过程的一部分。

sentences.en: becoming a happy single person in an older age.
sentences.zh: （成为一个快乐的年长单身人士的过程的一部分。）

sentences.en: I believe that most of your research is with people in the U.S., right?
sentences.zh: 我相信您的研究大多是针对美国人的，对吧？

sentences.en: We've conducted studies with people in the U.S., with Europeans.
sentences.zh: 我们已经对美国人和欧洲人进行了研究。

sentences.en: We've done a little bit of data collection in Korea, but we haven't really expanded out culturally beyond that.
sentences.zh: 我们在韩国也进行了一些数据收集，但我们并没有真正超越这一点进行文化上的扩展。

sentences.en: Are there cultural differences then in the research that you've done?
sentences.zh: 那么在您的研究中是否存在文化差异？

sentences.en: Have you found in other countries that there is a difference in singlehood, how it's experienced and how it's perceived?
sentences.zh: 您在其他国家是否发现单身生活在体验和感知上存在差异？

sentences.en: You know, I would say that so far, we haven't collected enough data to be able to answer that question well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会说到目前为止，我们还没有收集到足够的数据来很好地回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I think it is such an important question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say so far with the research that we've been conducting in Korea, we've been surprised at the similarities across the two cultures.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会说到目前为止，通过我们在韩国进行的研究，我们对两种文化之间的相似之处感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So, for example, when you ask single people, you know, what are your most important
sentences.zh: 例如，当你问单身人士，你最重要的

sentences.en: life priorities in both Korea and in the West where we've collected data, they say my most important priorities are my family and my health.
sentences.zh: 生活优先事项是什么时，在韩国和我们收集数据的西方国家，他们都说我最重要的优先事项是我的家庭和我的健康。

sentences.en: And they say that my least important priorities, at least of the ones that we ask them, are sex and dating.
sentences.zh: 他们说我最不重要的优先事项，至少在我们询问的那些中，是性和约会。

sentences.en: And that was something that was consistent across those two countries.
sentences.zh: 这在两国之间是一致的。

sentences.en: But one of the things that we've speculated about, and there has been a little bit of research in other labs about, is the role that family plays in single people's lives across
sentences.zh: 但我们推测的一件事，以及其他实验室进行的一点研究，是家庭在单身人士生活中所扮演的角色，跨越了

sentences.en: different cultures.
sentences.zh: 不同的文化。

sentences.en: You know, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，美国。

sentences.en: in particular is unique.
sentences.zh: 尤其是独特的。

sentences.en: It is, you know, by some measures, literally the most individualistic country in the world, which means that it's a system where your family doesn't
sentences.zh: 你知道，从某些衡量标准来看，它确实是世界上最崇尚个人主义的国家，这意味着在这个体系中，你的家庭并不会

sentences.en: have a lot of say in what you're dating and your marriage life is.
sentences.zh: 对你的约会和婚姻生活有太多的发言权。

sentences.en: That's really unusual.
sentences.zh: 这真的很不寻常。

sentences.en: In most countries around the world, family has a pretty big say about, you know, are you dating?
sentences.zh: 在世界上大多数国家，家庭对你是否在约会这件事上有着相当大的发言权，你知道的，

sentences.en: Who are you dating?
sentences.zh: 你在和谁约会？

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And so, it would make sense that that would lead to some kind of intense dynamics for single people in these more collectivistic kinds of countries where we would
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些更崇尚集体主义的国家里，单身人士面临某种强烈的动态压力也就说得通了，因为我们

sentences.en: expect because there's these cultural norms around you're a representative of our family, you're
sentences.zh: 预期由于存在着“你是家庭代表”这样的文化规范，你

sentences.en: supposed to be getting married, you're making us look bad by not getting married, that there could be
sentences.zh: 应该结婚，不结婚会让我们丢脸，所以他们可能会

sentences.en: some particular pressure on them to not be single, even if that in their heart is what they want to be.
sentences.zh: 承受某种特殊的压力而不能保持单身，即使那正是他们内心想要的。

sentences.en: So, I think that's going to be a really important direction for future research.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这将是未来研究的一个非常重要的方向。

sentences.en: We don't have a lot to say about that yet.
sentences.zh: 我们目前对此还没有太多定论。

sentences.en: Are you finding differences between the sexes?
sentences.zh: 你发现性别之间有什么差异吗？

sentences.en: Are single men happier than single women or vice versa?
sentences.zh: 单身男性比单身女性更快乐，还是反之？

sentences.en: We've been surprised in that regard.
sentences.zh: 在这方面我们感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, we have looked at gender differences in a number of our studies and haven't found a lot of differences between men and women.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在多项研究中考察过性别差异，并没有发现男性和女性之间有太大的不同。

sentences.en: I know that there's some sort of cultural tropes that men in particular as they get old are going to really struggle with singlehood.
sentences.zh: 我知道存在某种文化偏见，认为男性尤其是随着年龄增长，会非常难以适应单身生活。

sentences.en: Generally speaking, the data so far are more equivocal on that.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，目前的数据对此更为模棱两可。

sentences.en: You know, it does seem to be true that men, when they're single, struggle more than women do with social support.
sentences.zh: 你知道，男性在单身时，在社会支持方面确实比女性更挣扎，这似乎是真的。

sentences.en: So, that men will tend to have like less supportive friendships, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，男性往往拥有较少的支持性友谊，例如。

sentences.en: And so, that can be a bit of a struggle for them.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对他们来说可能是一个小小的挣扎。

sentences.en: But generally speaking, the data that we've been looking at, the numbers in terms of like how on average are you happy with singlehood,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我们一直在观察的数据，即关于平均而言你对单身生活有多满意的数字，

sentences.en: for example, there doesn't tend to be a lot of difference.
sentences.zh: 例如，往往没有太大的差异。

sentences.en: What we suspect is that underneath those numbers, the content of people's experiences might be different.
sentences.zh: 我们怀疑在这些数字背后，人们体验的内容可能有所不同。

sentences.en: So, you know, for example, if you were a single woman, there's going to be different stereotypes about you than if you're a single man, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，举个例子，如果你是一位单身女性，关于你的刻板印象会与单身男性不同，对吧？

sentences.en: Like women, for example, are seen as cold if they're single.
sentences.zh: 比如女性，如果她们单身，会被视为冷漠。

sentences.en: And that might not necessarily be the case for men.
sentences.zh: 而男性则未必如此。

sentences.en: And there are some negative words that define women who are single, like spinster.
sentences.zh: 而且有一些负面词汇用来定义单身女性，比如“老处女”。

sentences.en: There's nothing quite equivalent for a man.
sentences.zh: 对于男性来说，并没有完全对等的词。

sentences.en: No, there's not.
sentences.zh: 不，确实没有。

sentences.en: Not yet, anyways.
sentences.zh: 至少目前还没有。

sentences.en: A few moments ago, you talked about attachment in singlehood.
sentences.zh: 刚才你谈到了单身生活中的依恋关系。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you could talk a little bit more about attachment theory and how that relates to singlehood and the work that you do.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能多谈谈依恋理论，以及它与单身生活和你所做的工作有何关联。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So attachment theory is, you know, basically a theory to explain why is it that some people are more comfortable getting close to others than other people are?
sentences.zh: 依恋理论基本上是一种解释为什么有些人比其他人更乐于与他人亲近的理论。

sentences.en: You know, the original development of theory had this very psychodynamic kind of a bent to it where the idea was you get
sentences.zh: 你知道，该理论最初的发展带有非常强烈的心理动力学倾向，其观点是你

sentences.en: treated a particular way in childhood and that teaches you how to interact with other people.
sentences.zh: 在童年时期受到某种方式的对待，这教会了你如何与他人互动。

sentences.en: More recently, there's been some longitudinal research that has looked at, you know, how much of this is really rooted in childhood.
sentences.zh: 最近，有一些纵向研究考察了，你知道，其中有多少真正植根于童年。

sentences.en: And there's some questions about that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点还存在一些疑问。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think that that part of attachment being about childhood is a little bit in flux these days.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为依恋关系与童年有关的那部分在今天看来还有些不确定。

sentences.en: But what is absolutely clear from an attachment theory perspective is that you can measure stable personality differences in how people relate to other people.
sentences.zh: 但从依恋理论的角度来看，绝对清楚的是，你可以衡量人们在与他人建立关系方式上的稳定人格差异。

sentences.en: So the two dimensions on which we typically think of differences in people about how they relate to others are these two variables that
sentences.zh: 因此，我们通常认为人们在与他人建立关系方面存在差异的两个维度是这两个变量，

sentences.en: we call anxious attachment and avoidant attachment.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为焦虑型依恋和回避型依恋。

sentences.en: So anxiously attached people, I mean, these are the kinds of people who you would sort of colloquially think about is the needy and clingy type.
sentences.zh: 焦虑型依恋者，我的意思是，这些人就是你通俗理解的那种需要关注和粘人的类型。

sentences.en: So the person who, you know, needs a lot of attention, they want validation because they don't feel so great about themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，需要大量关注的人，他们想要认可，因为他们对自己感觉不是很好。

sentences.en: But they also feel really hesitant in approaching other people because they're really scared of getting rejected.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也对接近他人感到非常犹豫，因为他们非常害怕被拒绝。

sentences.en: So they can have this kind of strong approach avoidance dynamic going on in their relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在人际关系中可能会有这种强烈的“接近-回避”动态。

sentences.en: With avoidantly attached people, avoidantly attached people, they're the kinds of people who you would think of as the independent type.
sentences.zh: 对于回避型依恋者，回避型依恋者，他们就是你认为的那种独立类型的人。

sentences.en: They're the person who's likely to tell you that they don't really need relationships.
sentences.zh: 他们是那种很可能会告诉你他们并不真正需要人际关系的人。

sentences.en: You know, I always like to say that, you know, if you're the person when there's eight bags of groceries to carry from the car into the house that
sentences.zh: 你知道，我总是喜欢说，如果你是那种当有八袋杂货要从车里搬进屋子时，

sentences.en: you want to take them all by yourself, you might be avoidantly attached.
sentences.zh: 想要一个人全部搬完的人，你可能就是回避型依恋者。

sentences.en: They're the kinds of people who don't really like to be reliant on other people, don't like to get a lot of help from other people.
sentences.zh: 他们是那种不太喜欢依赖他人，不喜欢从他人那里获得太多帮助的人。

sentences.en: So we have a little bit of research looking at, you know, do these individual differences in how
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了一些研究，考察了，你知道，这些个体在如何

sentences.en: people relate to other people, are they related to how happy people are in singlehood?
sentences.zh: 与他人建立关系上的差异，是否与人们在单身生活中的幸福感有关？

sentences.en: And so it turns out that people who are more anxiously attached, and again, these are the needy and
sentences.zh: 结果发现，那些更倾向于焦虑型依恋的人，再说一次，这些就是那种需要关注和

sentences.en: clingy type, they have a bit of a sense that they can't quite get through life without other people.
sentences.zh: 粘人的类型，他们有一种感觉，觉得没有别人自己就无法过好生活。

sentences.en: They're not very happy with being single.
sentences.zh: 他们对单身并不感到快乐。

sentences.en: So single, anxiously attached people are relatively low in their overall life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 所以，单身的焦虑型依恋者在整体生活满意度上相对较低。

sentences.en: They're relatively low in how satisfied they are with singlehood.
sentences.zh: 他们对单身生活的满意度也相对较低。

sentences.en: So they feel like they really need a relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以他们觉得他们非常需要一段关系。

sentences.en: I mean, the unfortunate thing for anxiously attached people is that they also, when they do get into relationships, tend to have relatively low relationship satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对焦虑型依恋者来说不幸的是，当他们进入一段关系时，往往也会有相对较低的关系满意度。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like they have this story, if I just get into a relationship, I'll be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像他们有这样一个故事：如果我能进入一段关系，我就没问题了。

sentences.en: And it turns out that that doesn't quite work.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明这并不奏效。

sentences.en: And so that definitely goes back to what I was saying before, that there's, you know, some people
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对回到了我之前所说的，有，你知道，有些人

sentences.en: who probably need to work on themselves first before they're ready for a relationship.
sentences.zh: 可能在准备好进入一段关系之前，需要先完善自己。

sentences.en: And that might particularly be the anxiously attached people.
sentences.zh: 而这可能特别适用于焦虑型依恋者。

sentences.en: Avoidantly attached people are a bit of a curious case in that avoidantly attached people are not particularly unhappy about being single.
sentences.zh: 回避型依恋者是一个有点好奇的案例，因为回避型依恋者对单身并不特别感到不快乐。

sentences.en: So they're no less satisfied with singlehood than your more secure type of person.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对单身生活的满意度并不比你那种更安全型的人低。

sentences.en: But they do seem to be lower in overall life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但他们的整体生活满意度似乎确实较低。

sentences.en: So they're interesting to me because they say that they're not unhappy about being single.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对我来说很有趣，因为他们说他们对单身并不感到不快乐。

sentences.en: They don't report particularly wanting a romantic partner, but something is going on that's leading them to feel less happy in life overall.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有报告说特别想要一个浪漫伴侣，但有什么事情导致他们整体生活幸福感较低。

sentences.en: One of the things that we've speculated there, and this came from my graduate student and amazing collaborator,
sentences.zh: 我们推测的一点是，这来自于我的研究生和出色的合作者，

sentences.en: Eubin Park.
sentences.zh: 朴尤彬。

sentences.en: You know, her idea, which I think is a really good one, is that with avoidantly attached people, again, they like distance, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，她的想法，我认为非常好，是对于回避型依恋者，再说一次，他们喜欢距离，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't like to get too close to people, but that doesn't just apply to their romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢与人太亲近，但这不仅仅适用于他们的浪漫关系。

sentences.en: And as we talked about before, to be a happy single, it's going to help a lot to have close relationships with your family and with your friends.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前谈到的，要成为一个快乐的单身人士，与家人和朋友建立亲密关系会有很大帮助。

sentences.en: And avoidantly attached people struggle in those kinds of domains too, because they keep their emotional distance there.
sentences.zh: 而回避型依恋者在这些领域也感到挣扎，因为他们在那里保持着情感距离。

sentences.en: And there is some research that suggests that this is avoidantly attached people, even though it feels better or easier for them in the short term
sentences.zh: 确实有一些研究表明，这就是回避型依恋者，即使在短期内，回避这些关系

sentences.en: to avoid those kinds of relationships.
sentences.zh: 让他们感觉更好或更容易。

sentences.en: If you actually do like in an experimental study, kind of push them a little bit to get into an emotional, intimate situation.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的像在实验研究中那样，稍微推动他们进入一种情感亲密的情境。

sentences.en: I mean, I always say that for avoidantly attached people, intimacy is like exercise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总是说对于回避型依恋者，亲密关系就像锻炼。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel good in the moment, but it builds capacity over the long term, right?
sentences.zh: 当下感觉并不好，但从长远来看它能建立能力，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, they do seem to get something good out of those close interactions.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们似乎确实从这些亲密互动中得到了一些好处。

sentences.en: They just don't seem to be motivated to push themselves into them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是似乎没有动力去推动自己进入这些互动。

sentences.en: So, that's one reason we think that avoidantly attached people are kind of attracted to being single, because you can avoid all the problems and the conflicts that come
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们认为回避型依恋者倾向于单身的一个原因，因为你可以避免所有随之而来的问题和冲突

sentences.en: with relationships.
sentences.zh: 在关系中。

sentences.en: But the flip side of that is that you don't get the benefits of relationships.
sentences.zh: 但反面是，你无法获得关系带来的好处。

sentences.en: You've also looked at something called progression bias, which as I understand it is the tendency among people to stay in relationships, even when they're not that great.
sentences.zh: 你还研究过一种叫做“进展偏见”的东西，据我理解，这是人们倾向于留在关系中，即使关系并不那么好。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective, aren't we almost hardwired to try to stay coupled even when it's not optimal?
sentences.zh: 从进化角度来看，我们难道不是几乎被硬编码为即使在不理想的情况下也要保持结伴吗？

sentences.en: It's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, this is some work that I've done with my former PhD student, and she's now a professor at Western University, Samantha Joel.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我和我以前的博士生，现在是西安大略大学教授的Samantha Joel所做的一些工作。

sentences.en: And the idea with progression bias is it's kind of like I was talking about before when you get
sentences.zh: 关于进展偏见的想法，有点像我之前谈到的，当你进入

sentences.en: into a casual sexual relationship, and then it's all of a sudden you find yourself more and more committed.
sentences.zh: 一段随意的性关系，然后突然之间你发现自己投入得越来越多。

sentences.en: What we think is that we think that there's a couple of reasons why this might be, and one of them is definitely the evolutionary case that you're bringing up there.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这可能有几个原因，其中之一绝对是你提到的进化论案例。

sentences.en: Our thinking on this is our ancestors long, long ago, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对此的思考是，我们的祖先在很久很久以前，对吧？

sentences.en: If you think about hunter-gatherer groups living in relatively small numbers of people, that if you kind of took the online dating strategy of
sentences.zh: 如果你想想生活在相对较少人数的狩猎采集群体中，如果你采取那种在线约会策略，

sentences.en: swiping left on everyone until you came to your absolute perfect match, I mean, there's only 30 people that you could possibly date.
sentences.zh: 对每个人都向左滑，直到你遇到你绝对完美的匹配，我的意思是，你可能约会的只有30个人。

sentences.en: You might end up rejecting everybody, and you're not going to pass your genes down because you're not mating with anybody, right?
sentences.zh: 你最终可能会拒绝所有人，而你将无法传递你的基因，因为你没有与任何人交配，对吧？

sentences.en: Look, if the human heart is kind of built to just sort of fall for somebody and make that work relatively easily, then that might have
sentences.zh: 看，如果人类的心脏天生就是为了去爱上某人并相对容易地让它运作，那么这可能

sentences.en: been sort of a successful strategy for people living in those relatively small groups.
sentences.zh: 是生活在那些相对较小群体中的人们的一种成功策略。

sentences.en: And so, we think that it is true that people in relationships are kind of biased toward keeping
sentences.zh: 所以，我们认为确实，处于关系中的人们倾向于保持

sentences.en: the relationship going, sometimes even if it's not the happiest relationship, because that might have been evolutionarily useful.
sentences.zh: 关系继续，有时即使这不是最快乐的关系，因为这在进化上可能是有用的。

sentences.en: But having said that, we don't think that the evolution part of it is the only part of the story.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我们并不认为进化的部分是故事的全部。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of social and structural systems, as we've talked about today, that are also biased towards relationships, that give people the sense that you're supposed to
sentences.zh: 正如我们今天所谈到的，还有各种各样的社会和结构系统，也偏向于关系，让人们觉得你应该

sentences.en: be in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 处于一段关系中。

sentences.en: And one of the things that we argue in my lab is make it hard for people to notice sometimes if they're happier being single.
sentences.zh: 我们在我的实验室里争论的一点是，这使得人们有时很难注意到他们单身时是否更快乐。

sentences.en: You're not looking for that when you're raised in a society where you expect relationships to be what makes you happy.
sentences.zh: 当你成长在一个期望关系能让你快乐的社会中时，你不会去寻找那个。

sentences.en: So, we think that there's two really powerful forces happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们认为有两种非常强大的力量在发生作用。

sentences.en: We do think that the human heart kind of, you know, gets itself stuck in relationships sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我们确实认为人类的心有时，你知道，会陷入关系中。

sentences.en: But we also think there's a lot of social pressure to get into and to stay in relationships.
sentences.zh: 但我们也认为存在很大的社会压力去进入并保持在关系中。

sentences.en: Which raises the question of societal stigma then against singlehood, which it seems you're saying is pervasive.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了对单身生活的社会污名化问题，看起来你说这是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: Is that really a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 这真的是一件坏事吗？

sentences.en: It's certainly a bad thing for single people.
sentences.zh: 这对单身人士来说当然是一件坏事。

sentences.en: You know, if you're trying to – well, if you're trying to build a society where you want people to stay stuck in relationships, it's great.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你试图——好吧，如果你试图建立一个社会，你想让人们陷入关系中，那很好。

sentences.en: But if you're a single person who wants to be single and is living their best and happiest life as a single person, it can be a really negative force in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个想要单身并作为单身人士过着最好、最快乐生活的单身人士，这可能成为人们生活中非常负面的力量。

sentences.en: And I think that one of the problems with discrimination against single people is that to a certain extent, it's still kind of an acceptable stigma.
sentences.zh: 我认为歧视单身人士的问题之一在于，在某种程度上，这仍然是一种可接受的污名。

sentences.en: I think people have internalized the idea that there's something wrong with single people.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们已经内化了单身人士有什么问题的想法。

sentences.en: And so, it doesn't even feel like unfair discrimination when, for example, and this is
sentences.zh: 所以，这甚至感觉不像是不公平的歧视，例如，这是

sentences.en: something that data has shown, people are more likely to rent an apartment to somebody who's in a relationship than somebody who is single, right?
sentences.zh: 数据显示的，人们更有可能把公寓租给处于关系中的人，而不是单身的人，对吧？

sentences.en: That if you get into a big health crisis and your social support is your best friend, they may not be able to get into the emergency room with you.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到严重的健康危机，而你的社会支持是你的好朋友，他们可能无法和你一起进入急诊室。

sentences.en: But if it's your wife or your husband, there's no problem there whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 但如果是你的妻子或丈夫，那就完全没有问题。

sentences.en: So, it can create some really important barriers in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 所以，这会在人们的生活中制造一些非常重要的障碍。

sentences.en: Bella DePaulo is someone who's talked about this extensively and I think she makes a really good argument here that these are some forces that not
sentences.zh: Bella DePaulo是广泛谈论过这一点的人，我认为她在这里提出了一个非常好的论点，即这些力量不仅

sentences.en: only affect single people's lives negatively, but I think a lot of people are only just realizing that these are unfair stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 对单身人士的生活产生负面影响，而且我认为很多人才刚刚意识到这些是不公平的刻板印象。

sentences.en: Do you think that the pandemic affected how some people think about being single?
sentences.zh: 你认为疫情影响了人们对单身生活的看法吗？

sentences.en: And I'm asking because at the beginning of the pandemic, many people were strictly social distancing and
sentences.zh: 我这样问是因为在疫情初期，许多人严格保持社交距离，

sentences.en: there were lots of news stories about how social distancing was particularly difficult for single people, especially those who were living alone.
sentences.zh: 有很多新闻报道说社交距离对单身人士尤其困难，特别是那些独居的人。

sentences.en: Was that just a temporary blip that we're done with now that social distancing is over?
sentences.zh: 那只是一个我们现在已经结束的暂时性插曲吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think this is going to have some kind of lasting effect on how people treat and value relationships?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为这将对人们如何对待和重视关系产生某种持久的影响？

sentences.en: I think that's a very interesting question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of data on this point, so I'm just going to go ahead and speculate now.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点没有太多数据，所以我现在要进行推测。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think that the reason why more and more people have been living single is that we've been structuring society in a way that
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为越来越多的人选择单身的原因是，我们一直在以一种方式构建社会，

sentences.en: makes it easier and easier for people to do so.
sentences.zh: 使得人们更容易这样做。

sentences.en: That, you know, the economic system is set up in a way that we don't need to be as dependent on close others as we did 100 or 200 years ago.
sentences.zh: 即，你知道，经济体系的设置方式使得我们不需要像100或200年前那样依赖亲近的他人。

sentences.en: So, the people who really like their independence can do that in a practical kind of way now.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些真正喜欢独立的人现在可以以一种实际的方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: But I think that the pandemic was kind of a reminder of that, that, you know, it's not that more people are becoming
sentences.zh: 但我认为疫情是一种提醒，你知道，并不是因为社会趋势有什么必然正确之处，所以更多人变得

sentences.en: single because there's something inevitably correct about the societal move.
sentences.zh: 单身。

sentences.en: I think it's people are adjusting themselves to the society that they live in.
sentences.zh: 我认为是人们在适应他们所生活的社会。

sentences.en: And during the pandemic, when people were more housebound, you didn't have access to the kinds of social networks that make it easier to live as a happy single person.
sentences.zh: 而在疫情期间，当人们更多地被困在家里时，你无法获得那些使作为快乐单身人士生活更容易的社会网络。

sentences.en: So, you know, for example, I think a lot of the discourse around, you know, who was really struggling during the pandemic, a lot of this discourse is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，例如，我认为围绕着，你知道，谁在疫情期间真正挣扎的很多讨论，很多这种讨论是，你知道，

sentences.en: people with kids, for example, you know, how do you balance the workplace and kids and all this kind of stuff, all of which is totally valid.
sentences.zh: 有孩子的人，例如，你知道，你如何平衡工作场所和孩子以及所有这些事情，所有这些都是完全合理的。

sentences.en: You know, having kids during the pandemic was a real challenge.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在疫情期间生孩子是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: But when you look at the data as to who was the most happy versus who was the least happy
sentences.zh: 但当你查看关于谁最快乐与谁最不快乐的数据时

sentences.en: during the pandemic, it was people living with partners and children who are the most happy, right?
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，是与伴侣和孩子住在一起的人最快乐，对吧？

sentences.en: You might be stressed, but you're stimulated.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到压力，但你受到了刺激。

sentences.en: You're not bored.
sentences.zh: 你不会感到无聊。

sentences.en: The people who are having the hardest time were the people who are living by themselves, that there is something about just
sentences.zh: 最艰难的人是那些独自生活的人，关于这一点确实有些东西

sentences.en: not having any stimulation and social connection in your environment that can be really challenging.
sentences.zh: 环境中缺乏任何刺激和社交联系，这确实会带来很大的挑战。

sentences.en: So, I think that was something that got people to think twice anyways about, you know, how sustainable is a single life.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这至少让人们重新思考，单身生活究竟有多大的可持续性。

sentences.en: And then I think it's interesting to think about what are the future social structural changes that might drive people into different kinds of living circumstances.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，思考未来哪些社会结构性变化可能会促使人们进入不同的生活环境，是一件很有意思的事。

sentences.en: So, for example, you know, here in Toronto, rent and house prices are out of control.
sentences.zh: 比如，在多伦多这里，租金和房价已经失控了。

sentences.en: The people who might have been able to afford to live on their own in the past are going to be forced into more group living situations.
sentences.zh: 过去可能负担得起独自生活的人，未来将被迫进入更多的群体居住环境。

sentences.en: But maybe when you've got a roommate, that takes up some of the – or that accounts for some of the need that you might have had a romantic partner for, right?
sentences.zh: 但也许当你有了室友，这就能满足你原本可能需要伴侣来满足的部分需求，对吧？

sentences.en: So, maybe there's another force that leads people to be less motivated to be in romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许还有另一种力量导致人们对建立恋爱关系的动力减弱。

sentences.en: So, I think it's completely unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这完全是不可预测的。

sentences.en: You know, are people going to be living single more or be living single less?
sentences.zh: 人们未来是会更多地选择单身，还是更少地选择单身呢？

sentences.en: I think it really depends on, you know, what happens to society and what are the opportunities and challenges for single people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的取决于社会发生了什么，以及单身人士面临着怎样的机遇和挑战。

sentences.en: So, it's – I think that's the important thing to remember is that it's not just some, you know, amazing moral choice to live single or to not live single.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为重要的一点是，要记住单身或不单身，这不仅仅是一个了不起的道德选择。

sentences.en: All of us are trying to just get by in the society that we live in and that society is constantly changing.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在努力适应我们所处的社会，而这个社会正在不断变化。

sentences.en: This is a relatively young field with a lot of wide open questions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相对年轻的领域，还有许多未解之谜。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering what are some of the most important research questions that you still want to explore?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你目前最想探索的研究课题有哪些？

sentences.en: I'd say that the thing that is in the front of our mind and in my lab right now is that – and,
sentences.zh: 我想说，目前我和我的实验室最关注的问题是——而且，

sentences.en: you know, maybe this is a little bit because we came to singlehood research as relationship researchers.
sentences.zh: 也许这在一定程度上是因为我们是以关系研究者的身份进入单身研究领域的。

sentences.en: And so, I think that as we've been doing singlehood research, a lot of our focus has been on are they dating?
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为在我们进行单身研究的过程中，我们的很多关注点都集中在他们是否在约会？

sentences.en: Do they want to date?
sentences.zh: 他们想约会吗？

sentences.en: Are they having sex?
sentences.zh: 他们有性生活吗？

sentences.en: Do they want to have sex?
sentences.zh: 他们想有性生活吗？

sentences.en: And so, our focus has been this narrow kind of dating and sexual domain.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的关注点一直局限在约会和性这一狭窄领域。

sentences.en: But we've started to do some studies that I've alluded to a little bit where we're asking about single people's broader lives and
sentences.zh: 但我们已经开始做一些我之前提到过的研究，询问单身人士更广泛的生活状况，

sentences.en: we're finding out things like sex and dating is relatively low on their priority liSt. That, you know, things like their health, things like their workplace, for example,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，性生活和约会其实在他们的优先事项清单上排得比较靠后。比如，他们的健康、工作场所等，

sentences.en: are really important factors.
sentences.zh: 才是真正重要的因素。

sentences.en: So, I think because, in a sense, single people are defined as people who have the absence of a romantic relationship, that's led us to think that everything
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为在某种意义上，单身人士被定义为缺乏恋爱关系的人，这导致我们认为他们生活的方方面面

sentences.en: about their life surrounds a romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 都围绕着恋爱关系展开。

sentences.en: I think for a lot of happy singles, they don't even think about romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于许多快乐的单身人士来说，他们甚至根本不会去想恋爱关系。

sentences.en: There's a lot of other parts of their life that are more important.
sentences.zh: 他们生活中还有很多其他部分更为重要。

sentences.en: But I don't think we've done a good enough job of studying single people's lives holistically in that sense.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们在从整体上研究单身人士生活方面做得还不够好。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like a really interesting area to be researching.
sentences.zh: 听起来这是一个非常有趣的研究领域。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. McDonald.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天接受我的采访，麦克唐纳博士。

sentences.en: I really appreciated your taking the time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您抽出时间。

sentences.en: It's been my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org，或者在 Apple、Stitcher 以及您获取播客的任何平台收听《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学会为您报道。
